Done. Summary of the work:

## Fault located
`packages/agent/src/harness/runtime/drive/tools.ts` → `recoverToolInvocation`. Recovery decided to replay a durable `effect_pending` call using only the *persisted* policy (`call.replay === "safe"`), ignoring the *current* tool declaration. Consequences:
- a tool changed to `replay: "never"` was replayed anyway;
- a tool that no longer existed was replayed with `tool === undefined`, clearing the durable checkpoint before `undefined.execute(...)` rejected at the effect boundary — throwing instead of settling as interrupted.

## Repair (minimal, 1 condition)
```ts
if (!cancelled && call.replay === "safe" && tool?.replay === "safe") {
```
Replay now requires persisted-safe **and** current-declaration-safe and non-cancelled; every other combination falls through to `readCheckpoint` + `interruptedOutcome`, preserving checkpoint content/details while never clearing the checkpoint or crossing the effect boundary.

## Regression added
`.prale-eval/regression.mjs` uses the read-only `subject.mjs` `createRecoverySubject` to exercise the real `recoverToolInvocation`/`interruptedOutcome` through boundary fakes, asserting 7 cases: both-safe replay (exact event order, real effect result, recovery marking); changed declaration → interrupted; missing tool → interrupted (no throw, no execute); cancelled → interrupted; persisted `never` → interrupted; policy-less declaration → interrupted; missing tool + persisted `never` → interrupted. Interrupted cases assert checkpoint preservation, interruption marker, no `clear`, and no effect-boundary event.

## Validation
`node --experimental-vm-modules .prale-eval/regression.mjs` → exits 0 with all 7 cases passing. Reverting the guard reproduces the fault and the suite exits 1 with an `AssertionError` on the changed-declaration case. `node_modules` is absent (deps were not installed), so vitest/tsc suites could not run; that limitation is recorded in the result notes.
